Maine in 2025: HUD counts 20,823 people in Housing Choice Voucher households
In 2025, HUD reported that 11,926 Maine households used Housing Choice Vouchers, based on tenant reports it received.
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development counted 20,823 people in Maine households that used Housing Choice Vouchers and whose tenant reports it received in 2025. The number of people was down 2,267 from 23,090 in 2024. Those households numbered 11,926.
HUD reported 15,639 Housing Choice Vouchers available in Maine, and 77% of them were in use, down 2 percentage points from 79% in 2024.
Of those households, 11% were headed by a person HUD classifies as a racial or ethnic minority. Households paid an average of $466 a month toward rent and utilities, up $25 from $441 in 2024, and their average household income was $18,279 a year, up $743 from $17,536 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
Families receiving Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists in 2024, according to the . That average covers families who obtained assistance, not applicants still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
